Remaining on that very path,
There is nothing wonderful about that.
But those who rely on the Buddha's path
And speak of everything as impermanent,
While grasping for the excellence of things through dispute—
That station is despised.

When, after investigating, one does not find
Anything that can be called "this" or "that,"
Which wise person would say
In dispute that "this" or "that" is true?

Those who, without reliance,
Are attached to a self or the world—
Alas, they are carried away by views
Such as "permanent," "impermanent," and so on.

Those who accept things
As established in suchness through reliance,
How could the faults of "inference" and so forth
Not arise for them?

Those who accept things through reliance
As being like the moon in water,
Neither real nor false—
They are not carried away by views.

If there is the acceptance of things as real,
Then the terrible and malicious views
Arising from desire and hatred will emerge,
And conduct arising from them will follow.

That acceptance is the cause of all views.
Without it, afflictions do not arise.
Therefore, if that is thoroughly known,
Views and afflictions will be completely purified.

If you wonder, "Who knows that
While there is the acceptance of things as real?"
One who sees dependent origination sees
That what is born through reliance is unborn.

This was taught by the Supreme Knower of Suchness.
It overcomes false knowledge.
The process of attachment, dispute, and so forth
Arising from "truth," "untruth," and "falsehood,"
Proceeds from attachment.

Those of great nature
Have no position and no dispute.
For those who have no position,
How could there be a counter-position?

Having found any kind of station,
One will be seized by the deceptive, poisonous snake of afflictions.
Those whose minds have no station
Will not be seized.

For those whose minds have a station,
Why would the great poison of afflictions not occur?
They will be seized by the snake of afflictions.
By perceiving things as true, children

Are attached to reflections.
In the same way, because the world is confused,
head:
If those who speak of existence
Remain attached to the excellence of things,
tail: It becomes trapped in the snare of objects.
old_translation:
<meta>continues from previous page</meta>
...dwell by adhering to the excellence of things, they are staying on that very path; there is nothing wonderful about that. 

Those who, depending on the Buddha's path, speak of everything as impermanent but grasp at things as excellent through dispute—that dwelling is to be despised. 

When, having analyzed "is it this or that," nothing is perceived, what wise person would say "this or that dispute is true"? 

Those who, without depending <note>on reasoning</note>, adhere to a self or the world—alas, they are carried away by views of permanence, impermanence, and so on! 

Those who wish to establish that things exist in reality by depending on them—how will the faults of such reasons and so on not arise for them? 

Those who accept that things dependently arise like the moon in water—neither real nor false—are not carried away by views. 

If there is an acceptance of entities, then the terrible and wicked views from which attachment and hatred arise will occur. Actions will arise from that. 

That is the cause of all views. Without it, afflictions do not arise. Therefore, if that is thoroughly known, views and afflictions are thoroughly purified. 

If one asks "By what is that known?", it is the one who sees dependent origination. The Supreme Knower <note>the Buddha</note> said that what is dependently born is unborn. 

To those who are overwhelmed by false knowledge, the sequence of grasping at "true" and "false" in what is not true, and of disputes and so on, will arise from attachment. 

Those great-souled ones have no position and no dispute. For those who have no position, how could there be an opposing position? 

Having found any place to dwell, one's mind will be seized by the deceptive, poisonous snake of the afflictions. Those who have no place to dwell will not be seized. 

For those whose minds have a place to dwell, why would the great poison of the afflictions not occur? They will be seized by the snake of the afflictions. By perceiving the world as true, the foolish are attached to it, like being attached to a reflection. Likewise, the world is deluded.
